title: Breaking the Memory Wall for Heterogeneous Federated Learning via Progressive Training

problem.claim: Federated learning must support collaborative model training on resource-constrained devices despite the high memory requirements of model training.

gap.claim: Most existing federated learning research assumes that participating devices have sufficient resources for training.

contributions.claim: ProFL partitions a model into architecture-based blocks and progressively trains them, freezing converged front blocks before training subsequent blocks.
ProFL uses model shrinking and model growing stages with output modules and initialization parameters to preserve block feature representations during progressive training.
ProFL proposes a scalar-perspective metric to assess each block's learning status and guide freezing and progression to the next block.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present ProFL as a new framework and describe the block-learning-status metric as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that ProFL reduces peak memory footprint by up to 57.4%.
The authors report that ProFL improves model accuracy by up to 82.4%.
The authors report theoretical convergence analysis and extensive experiments on representative models and datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated learning enables privacy-preserving collaborative training across devices.
Existing work commonly assumes adequate device resources, while training memory requirements hinder deployment on constrained devices.
ProFL progressively trains architecture-based model blocks, freezing converged blocks so the model grows over time.
Model shrinking, model growing, output modules, initialization parameters, and a block-status metric support feature preservation and safe progression.
The authors report convergence theory, experiments, reduced peak memory footprint, and improved accuracy.

unknowns: Specific models, datasets, baselines, and experimental configurations are not identified.
Communication overhead, training time, and resource trade-offs are not reported.
The abstract does not provide details sufficient to assess the convergence proof or independently verify the reported results.
